title: Media
tagline: Turn lectures, courses and recordings into material you can search, ask about and review

row.deleteDesc: It moves to the Library trash together with its transcript and watch progress. You can restore it from the trash.

import.dropHint: Drop to import audio or video
import.skipped_one: Skipped {{count}} file that isn't audio or video
import.skipped_other: Skipped {{count}} files that aren't audio or video
import.notMedia_one: The selected file isn't audio or video
import.notMedia_other: None of the {{count}} selected files are audio or video

empty.title: Import your first lecture
empty.transcribe: Transcripts: turn a lecture into timed subtitles, search while you watch and tap a line to jump there.
empty.ask: Ask as you watch: ask about this course and get answers with [Media@time] citations that jump back.
empty.review: Handouts and practice: build an illustrated handout note, then make flashcards and questions from what was taught.
empty.subtitleNote: Already have subtitles (.srt / .vtt / Bilibili .json)? Import the media, then pick “Import subtitle file” in its row menu and skip the transcription cost.

study.notFound: This media file can't be found. It may have been deleted.

handout.intro: A handout turns the transcript into a sectioned note with key frames, and each section links back to its moment in the video.
handout.wordHint: You can export a note to Word from the note editor.

ask.intro: Opens a new chat with this lecture attached and the Course study skill on. Answers come from the transcript with citations you can jump to.
ask.needTranscript: No transcript yet. Transcribe or import subtitles first for better answers.

quick.moment: Ask about what I just watched
quick.momentHint: Brings in the last minute of transcript before the playhead, no need to give the time
quick.keyPoints: List key points and hard parts

prompt.summary: Summarize the lecture “{{name}}” in the order it was taught, as bullet points, each with its timestamp citation.
prompt.keyPoints: List the key points and difficult parts of the lecture “{{name}}”, explain why each difficult part is easy to get wrong, and add timestamp citations.
prompt.moment:
I didn't quite get the part of “{{name}}” starting at {{ref}}. Using the transcript below, explain what was said and why, with an example if it helps, and cite timestamps.

{{quote}}
prompt.momentNoTranscript: I didn't quite get the minute of “{{name}}” after {{ref}}. Read the transcript for that time range, explain it clearly, and cite timestamps.

ask.citationHint: Timestamps in answers are clickable and jump the player to that moment.

practice.intro: Make cards and questions from this lecture's transcript: cards are generated in the background; questions open in chat for you to confirm.
practice.cardsHint: Generates cards from the transcript without opening a chat. They go into flashcard review, with a link back to the video
practice.questionsHint: Questions go to Question sets for practice and review

prompt.cards: Make flashcards from the transcript of the lecture “{{name}}”: cover the core concepts, definitions and common mistakes, about 10 cards, each citing its timestamp as the source.
prompt.questions: Create a question set from the transcript of the lecture “{{name}}”: mostly multiple choice, fill-in and short answer, 5-10 questions, each with the answer, an explanation and its timestamp citation.
prompt.checkpoints: Create in-lecture checkpoints for “{{name}}” as a new question set named “{{name}} · Checkpoints”: about one question every 5 minutes in teaching order, mostly single choice and true/false. Two thirds should make me think (why, what if, how it connects to an earlier idea) and one third should check recall of what was just taught. End each explanation with a new line citing the source as [媒体@{{id}}:mm:ss], using the moment the tested content is taught. Do not make up timestamps.

practice.cardsInChat: Make cards in chat (add your own requirements)
practice.checkpointsHint: About one question every 5 minutes, anchored to the moment. They pop up as you watch and show on the progress bar

ledger.title: This lecture
ledger.empty: No cards or questions from this lecture yet. Use the buttons above to make some.
